topic.title: Task Activity View
topic.shortdesc: Use the Task Activity view to review task-level messages, track file changes, and open earlier or current file versions.

body.p: Click Task Activity in the left stripe to open the Task Activity view for the current review task.
Task Activity shows task messages and file activity. Each activity includes an icon that shows the type of activity, the name of the user who made the change, and when it happened.

You can use the Filter button in the top-right corner to open a pop-up control where you can select the Type of activity to show (All, Messages, or Changes) and you can select a particular Author to show the activity for that particular collaborator.
For added files, click the file name in Task Activity to open the file. For changed files, click the file name to open a comparison view that shows the changes for that activity.

For changed files, if you hover over the file name, you can click Open latest version to open the current version of the file in the visual editor. You can also click the vertical ellipsis (3 vertical dots) on the far right to access the following actions:

dlentry.dd: Opens the current version of the selected file in the visual editor.
Opens a comparison between the selected file change and the latest version of the file.
Opens the version of the file that existed when the selected file change was made.
Opens a comparison between the selected file change and the previous version of the file.

section.title: Communicating With Other Collaborators
section.p: To communicate with other collaborators in the review task, enter your message in the text box at the bottom of the Task Activity view and click the Add message button when you are finished. Task messages are attached to the review task, not to individual files. To annotate a specific file, use the Add Comment button in the editor.

You can mention other users (or yourself) in the comment by typing @ and choosing a person from the resulting drop-down list. The results of mentioning someone are as follows:
Mentioning the Current User - If you mention yourself in the message, your name is displayed with an orange color in the activity stream.
Mentioning an Existing Task Collaborator - If you mention someone who is already a collaborator on the task, the system records the activity message and sends a notification email to the mentioned user. The notification email includes a link that directs them to the particular message where they were mentioned.
Mentioning an Organization Member Who is not an Existing Task Collaborator - If you mention someone who is a member of the organization but not yet a collaborator on the task, the system adds that person as a collaborator on the task, records the activity message, and sends a notification email to the mentioned user. The notification email includes a link that directs them to the particular message where they were mentioned.
